result.summary: This residential street features townhouses with integrated garages, resulting in frequent driveway curb cuts that create numerous conflict points along the narrow sidewalk. The environment lacks dedicated pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crossings, traffic calming, or a visible sidewalk on both sides of the roadway.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is frequently interrupted by garage entrances, creating many points where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left side of the street where townhouses are located.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking on both sides of the narrow street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the mid-ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Continuous Sidewalk
hazards.description: A clear, paved sidewalk is not visible on the right side of the street, potentially forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street behind the parked cars.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or chicanes to ensure low vehicle speeds in this residential environment.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks to provide designated and visible locations for pedestrians to cross the street.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk and on-street parallel parking. While the pedestrian path is clear, the environment lacks marked crossings at the visible intersection, and sightlines are partially obstructed by mature trees and solid fencing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction (Vegetation and Fencing)
hazards.description: The large tree and tall red fence at the corner may block sightlines between drivers approaching the stop sign and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the intersection

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction (Parked Vehicle)
hazards.description: The parked car obscures the lower half of the sidewalk, potentially hiding small children from the view of passing motorists.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and prevent parking too close to the corner.

result.summary: The image depicts a T-intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk across the minor street. The environment lacks safety buffers between the walkway and the road, and the existing crosswalk markings are significantly degraded.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings across the side street are heavily worn, making the crossing less visible to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, crossing the street the camera is on.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane without any physical or distance buffer from moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the foreground street.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and slow down turning traffic at the intersection.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer, which enhances safety. However, the lack of marked crosswalks at the stop-controlled intersection and the presence of multiple residential driveways increase the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection Crossing
hazards.description: There is no marked crosswalk at the intersection where the stop sign is located, making pedestrian movements less predictable for drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the intersection.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: Multiple garage entrances on the right require vehicles to cross the sidewalk, creating potential conflict points.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the residential building is located.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalk markings at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install or upgrade curb ramps at the intersection to ensure the sidewalk is accessible to all users.
